This is kind of a random sampling of organizations spanning the entire space from evaluations of specific models to evaluations of practices to holistic judgments based on a broad range of evidence. And the goal of all this is to get to a world where a developer can say something about how their systems are developed and external actors can verify that is true. Ideally eventually connecting with this kind of shared sense of what is good enough from a safety perspective. What have we decided collectively is a level of evidence we expect or a level of risk we're willing to tolerate.
turns.zh: 所以，有了某种安全标准，下一步就是验证公司是否达到该标准，对吧？我们需要某种方式来判断开发者是否达到该标准。我们很快会讨论执行机制，但所有这些都依赖于某种可见性。所以这可以是前几节讨论的透明度措施的自然延伸。但它也确实需要额外的工作，对吧？或者你可能需要进行审计，以确认实施是否确实按描述进行，流程是否确实如某人声称的那样实施。许多组织在这个领域工作，进行某种组合的评估、评价和验证。其中许多最终有兴趣提供验证功能。这是一个随机抽样的组织，涵盖从特定模型的评估到实践评估再到基于广泛证据的整体判断的整个领域。所有这一切的目标是达到一个世界，开发者可以说明他们的系统是如何开发的，外部行为者可以验证这是真的。理想情况下最终与这种共享的安全视角下什么是足够好的感觉相联系。我们集体决定了我们期望的证据水平或我们愿意容忍的风险水平。

turns.en: Finally, with those pieces in place, you also need an actual source of pressure to push developers to deploy only or develop controllable systems. I'll go through a bunch of mechanisms here. Sort of an escalating spectrum, right? You have voluntary action. Companies contain a bunch of employees and executives and governance bodies who have some interest in doing the right thing. And so the first line you might take is just hopefully companies will do the right thing. And clarifying what the right thing is helps with that. It becomes much easier though as that becomes a norm and standard within industry as it's natural to say are we meeting best practice? And you can look at your competitors and say are we doing at least as well as they're doing, are we lagging behind? That can be a natural source or like cause for pressure that can escalate beyond industry to political pressure and public pressure. Right? As we clarify here is what a reasonable developer does, it becomes increasingly natural for someone to say are you meeting your obligations when you're developing this technology that can go further towards legal pressure which might take the form of liability or in very extreme cases even injunctive relief. Right? If there is a sense of what a developer needs to do in order to manage risk and a developer is not doing that, that creates a natural hook. Their existing authorities, right? Even without any new laws, both state and federal governments in the US and governments elsewhere, maybe to a lesser extent, have some power to intervene on unsafe AI development. There's beyond that the prospect of passing new laws, right? So, you should not think of these laws as encoding specific practices, right? the specific safety bar, but you should think of them as taking steps like empowering a regulator to actually turn what our industry best practices into binding requirements. And then we'll talk in a minute about international pressure. So briefly reviewing where we stand today on laws, I'll talk about two categories.
turns.zh: 最后，有了这些部分，你还需要一个实际的压力来源，推动开发者只部署或开发可控的系统。我将在这里介绍一系列机制。这是一个逐步升级的谱系，对吧？你有自愿行动。公司包含一群员工、高管和治理机构，他们对做正确的事情有一定兴趣。所以你可能采取的第一道防线就是希望公司会做正确的事。澄清什么是正确的事有助于这一点。然而，当这成为行业内的规范和标准时，就会变得容易得多，因为自然会说我们是否符合最佳实践？你可以看看竞争对手，说我们至少做得和他们一样好吗，我们落后了吗？这可以是一个自然的压力来源，可以升级到行业之外的政治压力和公众压力。对吧？当我们澄清什么是合理的开发者行为时，有人越来越自然地说，你在开发这项技术时是否履行了义务，这可以进一步走向法律压力，可能采取责任的形式，或在非常极端的情况下甚至禁令救济。对吧？如果有一种感觉，开发者需要做什么来管理风险，而开发者没有这样做，那就创造了一个自然的钩子。他们现有的权力，对吧？即使没有任何新法律，美国州和联邦政府以及其他地方的政府，也许程度较轻，都有一些权力干预不安全的 AI 开发。除此之外，还有通过新法律的前景，对吧？所以，你不应该认为这些法律编码了具体实践，对吧？具体的安全标准，但你应该认为它们采取了诸如授权监管机构将行业最佳实践转化为具有约束力的要求的步骤。然后我们稍后会讨论国际压力。所以简要回顾一下我们今天在法律方面的立场，我将讨论两个类别。

ts.sec: US State Bills and EU AI Act

turns.en: One are state bills in the US. These are particularly relevant because much development occurs in the US. Much of it is regulated by California in particular. Existing laws tend to require public safety policies of some kind, to protect whistleblowers who disclose violations of those policies, to require disclosure of incidents. So if something happens that causes harm or maybe is this extreme violation of policy, and in many cases these eventually require audits, they eventually require third parties to confirm that developers are in fact implementing the policies they say they're implementing. So these are mechanisms that can support this verification step. They can support this transparency step.
turns.zh: 一是美国的州法案。这些法案尤其重要，因为大量开发发生在美国，而其中很多又特别受加州监管。现有法律往往要求制定某种公共安全政策，保护披露违反这些政策行为的举报人，要求披露事件。所以如果发生了造成伤害的事情，或者可能是这种极端的政策违反，而且在许多情况下，这些最终要求审计，最终要求第三方确认开发者确实在执行他们声称正在执行的政策。因此，这些机制可以支持这个验证步骤，可以支持这个透明度步骤。

turns.en: The EU AI Act actually goes significantly further, and particularly the code of practice, a mechanism for compliance with the EU AI Act. So this actually requires specific evaluations, imposes like minimal standards of care for security and safety, requires risk assessments and so on. This is the timeline of implementation. As you can see, the EU AI Act has recently become enforceable, or the AI office recently got the ability to enforce. State laws have been coming into force over the last year, and auditing requirements tend to be a little bit further in the future.
turns.zh: 欧盟《人工智能法案》实际上走得更远，尤其是实践准则，这是一种遵守欧盟《人工智能法案》的机制。所以这实际上要求具体的评估，施加类似最低限度的安全与安保照护标准，要求风险评估等等。这是实施时间表。如你所见，欧盟《人工智能法案》最近变得可执行，或者人工智能办公室最近获得了执行能力。州法律在过去一年里陆续生效，而审计要求往往在更远的未来。

turns.en: One of the most challenging dimensions of this picture is international coordination. Right? The goal is to ensure that frontier AI, wherever it is, is adequately controlled, that defenders have access to trustworthy AI. And so if you are a state or a country looking at how you're going to regulate this technology, you naturally fear falling behind if you slow down. On the right, I have a graph of the performance of US frontier models and PRC frontier models. Right? This kind of graph is closely watched in the US. You see something like a gap of six months. Maybe it's bounced around a bit over the last few years. There is a lot of concern—if you look at rhetoric in the US, it is very centered on this concern that if we were to impose safety requirements, it would cause us to fall to second place. This is even worse because if in fact you're in this environment and an adversary does not implement similar safety policies, you haven't even succeeded at reducing risk. Right? This argument I mentioned at the beginning: if I don't do it, someone else will.
turns.zh: 这幅图景中最具挑战性的维度之一是国际协调。对吧？目标是确保前沿 AI，无论在哪里，都得到充分控制，确保防御者能够获得可信赖的 AI。所以，如果你是一个州或一个国家，正在考虑如何监管这项技术，你自然会担心如果放慢速度就会落后。右边，我有一张美国前沿模型和中国前沿模型性能的图表。对吧？这种图表在美国受到密切关注。你看到大约六个月的差距。也许过去几年里它有所波动。有很多担忧——如果你看美国的言论，它非常集中于这种担忧：如果我们施加安全要求，会导致我们跌至第二位。这甚至更糟，因为如果你实际上处于这种环境中，而对手没有实施类似的安全政策，你甚至没有成功降低风险。对吧？我一开始提到的这个论点：如果我不做，别人会做。

turns.en: So I'll talk on the next slide about how you might try and get some leverage here, like how international coordination might get off the ground. I will make a note before that which is to say that the dynamics of Chinese catch-up progress are extremely important for understanding the effects of US policy in the space. Right? So it is not the case that the US and China are separately racing to build this technology and it just so happens by coincidence that they move at almost exactly the same speed. Right? It's generally understood that in fact there are important catch-up dynamics. There is distillation of US models by Chinese competitors and there is diffusion of algorithmic ideas both within and between countries. Which means that if US development some month magically advanced by one month, the net effect would not be that forever more the US has one more month of lead, right? The net effect would be faster catch-up growth and that lead will decay. And we could debate what the time scale is, but the net effect of slowdowns is much smaller than it initially appears. You should not think of this as there's like a six-month budget of time that you could ever slow down before you get overtaken.
turns.zh: 所以我将在下一张幻灯片上讨论如何尝试在这里获得一些杠杆，比如国际协调如何起步。在此之前我要说明一点，即中国追赶的动态对于理解美国政策在该领域的效果极其重要。对吧？所以并不是美国和中国各自独立竞赛建造这项技术，然后碰巧以几乎完全相同的速度前进。对吧？人们普遍理解，实际上存在重要的追赶动态。中国竞争对手对美国模型进行蒸馏，算法思想在国内外扩散。这意味着，如果美国的开发某个月神奇地提前了一个月，净效果不会是永远美国多一个月的领先优势，对吧？净效果将是更快的追赶增长，而那个领先优势会衰减。我们可以争论时间尺度是多少，但放缓的净效果比最初看起来要小得多。你不应该认为存在一个六个月的预算时间，你可以在被超越之前放缓。

turns.en: So to talk a little bit about building blocks for international coordination, caveating that as we go on we are further into views of me as a researcher who is not in fact an expert in international relations. I think a natural starting point is having some shared understanding of risk. Right? You'd like to be in a regime where at least each state understands here's what we would do. Here's how we would like to regulate the technology. We have some understanding of if we were not facing international competition how we would approach this problem. And if the risk is sufficiently high, that becomes a rational strategy. Right? So if you're the US looking at this gap and saying maybe I run a 50% chance or if you end up in a world where it looks like you're running a greater than even chance of losing control, at some point it becomes rational for you and similarly for each other state to regulate the technology unilaterally. And I think this is an important point because in many worlds it will at some point if there is risk become clear that the risk is large. And so just this kind of shared understanding is quite valuable even if it only cuts off some of the most extreme scenarios.
turns.zh: 那么稍微谈谈国际协调的构建模块，需要说明的是，随着我们继续，这越来越是我作为研究者的观点，我实际上并非国际关系专家。我认为一个自然的起点是对风险有一些共同理解。对吧？你希望处于这样一种机制中：至少每个国家都明白我们会怎么做。我们希望如何监管这项技术。我们对如果没有面临国际竞争我们会如何处理这个问题有一些理解。如果风险足够高，那就会成为一种理性策略。对吧？所以如果你是美国，看着这个差距说也许我有 50% 的机会，或者如果你最终处于一个看起来你有超过一半机会失去控制的世界，那么在某个时刻，对你以及对每个其他国家来说，单方面监管这项技术就变得理性。我认为这是一个重要观点，因为在许多世界中，如果存在风险，某个时刻会清楚风险很大。所以这种共同理解非常有价值，即使它只切断一些最极端的情景。

turns.en: I think things get much better when you have some kind of visibility, right? So if for example the US has visibility into what PRC AI projects exist and moreover has visibility into whether those projects are meeting safety standards. So there's this implicit or explicit deterrent threat which is that if you build uncontrollable AI, right? Maybe right now I am bound by a regulatory regime that has been designed to reduce the risk of uncontrollable AI. I may say if I have visibility into your implementation and you build uncontrollable AI, I could simply have the threat in retaliation of abandoning my own regulatory regime or having this tit-for-tat process of if you skimp on safety, I skimp on safety. And from a game theoretic perspective with visibility that changes the picture enormously, right? So previously I was in a regime where there was a strong incentive for me to skimp because it slightly increased risk and significantly increased my competitive positioning. Whereas now if I were to skimp on safety, both it will only slightly improve my competitive position—right, because my adversary will respond by also skimping—but also means that the increase in risk is much larger.
turns.zh: 我认为当你拥有某种可见性时，情况会好得多，对吧？所以例如，如果美国能够看到中国存在哪些 AI 项目，而且能够看到那些项目是否达到安全标准。所以存在这种隐性或显性的威慑威胁，即如果你建造不可控的 AI，对吧？也许现在我受到一个旨在降低不可控 AI 风险的监管机制的约束。我可能会说，如果我能看到你的实施情况，而你建造了不可控的 AI，我可以简单地以放弃我自己的监管机制作为报复威胁，或者进行这种针锋相对的过程：如果你在安全上偷工减料，我也偷工减料。从博弈论的角度来看，有可见性会极大地改变局面，对吧？所以以前我处于一种机制中，我有强烈的动机偷工减料，因为这略微增加了风险，却显著提高了我的竞争地位。而现在，如果我在安全上偷工减料，一方面只会略微改善我的竞争地位——对吧，因为我的对手也会通过偷工减料来回应——但同时也意味着风险的增加要大得多。

turns.en: And maybe the last thing I will say is international pressure can make it much more costly for an entity not to play ball. Right? So you could be in a world where there is diplomatic or economic pressure on actors, where there is a broader international AI supply chain which can try and advantage people who are subscribing to reasonable policies, or in the limit you can imagine international adversaries disrupting AI projects. And so the net effect of all of this is you can be in a regime where both compliance with a reasonable risk governance strategy is much less costly and non-compliance is much more costly. And so I don't want to say any of this is easy. I just want to say that from a game theory perspective, it's not at all obvious whether the situation is sunk. These are things that require a lot of leg work to build this kind of shared understanding, to build this kind of visibility—both awareness of AI projects and inspections—and to build this kind of pressure. But all of them seem like plausible mechanisms.
turns.zh: 也许我要说的最后一点是，国际压力可以让一个实体不合作付出大得多的代价。对吧？所以你可能处于这样一个世界：对行为者存在外交或经济压力，存在更广泛的国际 AI 供应链，它可以试图让那些遵守合理政策的人获得优势，或者在极限情况下，你可以想象国际对手破坏 AI 项目。所以所有这些的净效果是，你可以处于这样一种机制：遵守合理的风险治理策略代价要小得多，而不遵守代价要大得多。所以我不想说这些中的任何一个是容易的。我只是想说，从博弈论的角度来看，情况是否已经注定一点也不明显。这些事情需要大量的基础工作来建立这种共同理解，建立这种可见性——既包括对 AI 项目的了解，也包括检查——并建立这种压力。但所有这些似乎都是可行的机制。

turns.en: All right. So I'm going to spend the rest of the talk discussing the need for more time. And so first on the object level, we currently do not have a very good understanding of whether systems are aligned. We are not able to adequately secure AI developments and operationally we are trying to build out the infrastructure for controlling AI systems but are still struggling because of a lack of time. So on the object level, we need more time to implement technical measures.
turns.zh: 好的。接下来我会用剩余的时间讨论为什么我们需要更多时间。首先在对象层面，我们目前对系统是否对齐还没有很好的理解。我们无法充分保障 AI 开发的安全，在操作层面我们正试图构建控制 AI 系统的基础设施，但由于时间不足仍然困难重重。所以在对象层面，我们需要更多时间来实施技术措施。

turns.en: From a governance perspective, I just talked about a lot of nice to haves. I talked about the idea of regulation or the idea of a shared bar on safety or a verification regime. All of those take time. Those are not the world we're in today. Those are the world we're trying to move to. But it is going to take time to get there.
turns.zh: 从治理角度，我刚才谈了很多锦上添花的东西。我谈到了监管的想法，或者共同安全标准的想法，或者核查机制。所有这些都需要时间。这些不是我们今天所处的世界，而是我们试图迈向的世界。但要达到那里需要时间。

turns.en: If we even bracket alignment and we think about the world more broadly, we are heading towards a world where there's incredible reliance on AI systems produced by a small number of tech companies and we do not have the institutions and mechanisms to keep those companies effectively accountable. So even if you ignore everything I've talked about on loss of control, we still need more time.
turns.zh: 即使我们把对齐问题搁置，更广泛地思考这个世界，我们正走向一个极度依赖少数科技公司生产的 AI 系统的世界，而我们没有机构和机制来有效问责这些公司。所以即使你忽略我讲过的所有关于失控的内容，我们仍然需要更多时间。

turns.en: And outside of the AI companies, there are a lot of ways in which society is going to need to adapt. Our institutions are going to need to adapt to new capabilities. Our economies are going to need to adapt. We're seeing simple examples like our cyber security is going to need to adapt even over the coming months. And all of this is true against a backdrop where AI progress may accelerate rapidly.
turns.zh: 而在 AI 公司之外，社会在许多方面都需要适应。我们的机构需要适应新能力。我们的经济需要适应。我们看到简单的例子，比如我们的网络安全甚至在未来几个月内就需要适应。而所有这些都发生在 AI 进步可能加速的背景下。

turns.en: Right? So this was the topic of yesterday. We may see a transformation over perhaps as little as a few months or a year from AI systems which are having a moderate impact in the world to AI systems which are superhuman across a broad range of domains. And I think if we see that kind of acceleration, if progress is much faster in the future than it has been in the past, I am extremely worried about our ability to get to good on any of these dimensions.
turns.zh: 对吧？这是昨天的话题。我们可能会看到在短短几个月或一年内，从对世界影响中等的 AI 系统转变为在广泛领域超越人类的 AI 系统。我认为如果我们看到那种加速，如果未来的进步比过去快得多，我非常担心我们在这些维度上取得良好结果的能力。

turns.en: So what is the minimal requirement? What is the minimal thing that would make me feel like we're on track? Um, I think at some point it is reasonably likely maybe over the next one to two years that further progress will look so risky that we would like to slow. Right? We could debate whether that's the case now. We can debate how high risk is now, but I think it is likely that at some point things will look like there is an immediate risk.
turns.zh: 那么最低要求是什么？什么是最低限度能让我觉得我们走在正轨上？嗯，我认为在某个时候，也许在未来一到两年内，进一步的发展会看起来风险太大，以至于我们想要放缓。对吧？我们可以争论现在是否已经是这种情况。我们可以争论现在风险有多高，但我认为很可能在某个时候情况会看起来存在直接风险。

turns.en: If we had the capacity to slow down later, right? If we had a reliable capacity to slow down later, then there would be a reasonable argument to wait and see. Right? There are real costs to trying to slow down. There are real issues with international competition. There are real reasons people want to deliver the technology faster. If we could see what happens later and adapt online, I think that would be a defensible option. The main problem is we don't really have the institutional and technical capacity to slow down when it counts.
turns.zh: 如果我们以后有能力放缓，对吧？如果我们以后有可靠的放缓能力，那么就有合理的理由观望。对吧？试图放缓是有实际成本的。国际竞争存在实际问题。人们希望更快地交付技术有实际原因。如果我们能看到以后会发生什么并在线适应，我认为那将是一个站得住脚的选择。主要问题是我们真的没有在关键时刻放缓的机构和技术能力。

turns.en: So I'm worried we're going to find ourselves in this world where further progress looks risky without the ability to slow effectively or without the ability to slow effectively without large costs. For example, maybe these are particularly important examples. I think we need mechanisms to identify risk. We need to understand whether the systems we are building are adequately controlled and aligned. If we're not able to do that, then it's good to tell a story about how we can slow down in the future. But we won't actually know when we get to that future.
turns.zh: 所以我担心我们会发现自己处于这样的世界：进一步的发展看起来有风险，却没有有效放缓的能力，或者没有在不付出巨大成本的情况下有效放缓的能力。例如，也许这些是特别重要的例子。我认为我们需要识别风险的机制。我们需要了解我们正在构建的系统是否得到充分控制和对齐。如果我们做不到这一点，那么讲述我们未来如何放缓的故事是好的。但当我们到达那个未来时，我们实际上不会知道。

turns.en: Even if we can identify risk, we need governance mechanisms, the kind of thing we've been talking about through this lecture, in order to be able to act collectively, right? We don't want to end up in the world where there's an awareness of risk, but there is a race to the bottom amongst AI developers. And it will take months or longer in order to actually build the machinery which would constrain that race to the bottom.
turns.zh: 即使我们能识别风险，我们还需要治理机制，也就是本讲座中一直在讨论的那种机制，以便能够集体行动，对吧？我们不希望最终陷入这样的世界：人们意识到风险，但 AI 开发者之间却逐底竞争。而实际构建约束这种逐底竞争的机制需要数月或更长时间。

turns.en: And then a slightly more subtle point that I think is perhaps actually the most important is that we need to be able to defend models and algorithms from theft. So I think a scenario from a US national security perspective that currently looks likely is that we will arrive at a point where further progress appears risky and there would be demand to slow but that there will be serious concerns or even a reasonably high probability that the underlying models or algorithms have leaked to adversaries.
turns.zh: 然后一个稍微更微妙、我认为也许实际上最重要的点是，我们需要能够保护模型和算法不被窃取。所以我认为从美国国家安全的角度来看，目前看起来可能的情景是，我们会到达一个点，进一步的发展显得有风险，会有放缓的需求，但存在严重担忧，甚至相当高的概率，底层模型或算法已经泄露给对手。

turns.en: And so we now face a dilemma between either proceeding with a technology we believe to be unsafe or risking competition from an adversary who has the same resources, who has taken those algorithms and perhaps is willing to tolerate higher risk. I think that is one of the most likely ways that we end up in an extremely bad situation.
turns.zh: 因此我们现在面临一个两难境地：要么继续推进我们认为不安全的技术，要么冒着与拥有相同资源、拿走了那些算法、也许愿意容忍更高风险的对手竞争的风险。我认为这是我们最终陷入极其糟糕境地的可能方式之一。

turns.en: So in light of that, my view is now we should probably slow down immediately until we actually have the infrastructure to slow down later, right? Until we have a high enough degree of security, governance, risk management that we are able to detect and react to future risks as they emerge.
turns.zh: 有鉴于此，我的观点是，我们现在可能应该立即放缓，直到我们真正拥有以后放缓的基础设施，对吧？直到我们拥有足够高的安全、治理、风险管理水平，能够发现并应对未来出现的风险。

turns.en: This is a letter signed by 1,400 employees from Frontier AI companies asking the US government to support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to what is it deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development. So this is not an uncommon sentiment, right? If you look through this list of signatories, it includes the chief scientists of most of the major AI companies. I think there's an understanding that we lack machinery we will need in order to be able to deliberately control the pace of progress.
turns.zh: 这是一封由前沿 AI 公司的 1,400 名员工签署的信，要求美国政府支持一项国际努力，开发所需的技术和治理工具，以刻意控制自动化 AI 发展的前沿步伐。所以这不是一种不常见的情绪，对吧？如果你看看这份签署者名单，它包括大多数主要 AI 公司的首席科学家。我认为人们理解我们缺乏必要的机制来刻意控制进步的步伐。

turns.en: I think I am going a little bit further here by saying that we may already be in the regime where our brakes are not good enough and we need to slow until we can improve our ability to slow in the future. Sometimes when you say that people imagine this would involve AI companies just sitting on their hands for a while while we try and sort things out. I want to emphasize that is not what we are talking about.
turns.zh: 我想我在这里说得更进了一步，说我们可能已经处于刹车不够好的状态，我们需要放缓，直到我们提高未来放缓的能力。有时当你这么说时，人们会想象这涉及 AI 公司只是袖手旁观一段时间，而我们试图解决问题。我想强调那不是我们所说的。

turns.en: Right? So if we talk about pacing, what we really mean is reducing investment in a couple areas, right? Not training GPT-7, not training bigger, smarter models and reduce investment in developing AI algorithms that could easily be stolen. So we're both not training GPT-7 and we're not developing the algorithms that would let you train GPT-7.
turns.zh: 对吧？所以当我们谈论节奏控制时，我们真正指的是减少几个领域的投资，对吧？不训练 GPT-7，不训练更大、更聪明的模型，并减少对开发容易被窃取的 AI 算法的投资。所以我们既不训练 GPT-7，也不开发能让你训练 GPT-7 的算法。

turns.en: And to instead increase investment in first improving safety, security, governance, right? Shoring up all of these technical measures we would need in order to be in a position to slow in the future, but also deploying the AI we have to help society prepare, to secure our infrastructure, to create actual products and beneficial applications, to generally close the gap between AI in the lab — where it is primarily driving this process of making AI ever smarter — and AI that is actually in people's lives, giving society time to adapt, helping harden infrastructure.
turns.zh: 转而增加投入，首先改善安全、安保与治理，对吧？把我们未来想要放慢脚步时所需要的所有技术措施都先夯实，同时也要部署我们现有的 AI，帮助社会做好准备，保护我们的基础设施，创造真正的产品和有益的应用，从总体上缩小这样一道鸿沟：一边是实验室里的 AI——它主要推动着让 AI 越来越聪明的进程——另一边是真正走进人们生活的 AI，从而给社会留出适应的时间，帮助加固基础设施。

turns.en: I think there's this general concern that the process of making smarter AIs can both be divorced from real-world utility and can be a major driver of risk. So when we say pacing, that's really what we mean. This sort of redirection of resources.
turns.zh: 我认为存在一种普遍的担忧：让 AI 变得更聪明的这个过程，既可能与现实世界的实用价值脱节，也可能成为风险的主要驱动因素。所以我们说“放慢节奏”，真正指的就是这个意思，也就是这种资源的重新调配。

turns.en: So to sum up, I think that we need governance to prevent the development of uncontrollable AI. This is a non-trivial challenge. I don't think it will be handled automatically by either markets or by liability or by unilateral restraint by altruistic developers.
turns.zh: 总结一下，我认为我们需要治理，来防止不可控 AI 的发展。这不是一个简单的挑战。我不认为市场、责任机制，或者利他开发者的单方面克制，会自动解决这个问题。

turns.en: In order to ensure that frontier AI is trustworthy for defenders, we need to understand the alignment, control, capabilities, and security of those systems. Getting to a shared bar on all of those dimensions will require transparency, public debate, verification, and ultimately enforcement mechanisms.
turns.zh: 为了确保前沿模型对防御方来说是可信的，我们需要理解这些系统的对齐、控制、能力与安全性。要在所有这些维度上达成一个共同的基准，就需要透明度、公开辩论、验证，以及最终的强制执行机制。

turns.en: And unfortunately, all of that seems like it is going to take more time than we have on the current trajectory, or there's significant risk at will. And so I believe we should be exploring policies both to accelerate the adoption of all of those, or progress on all of those dimensions, but also to buy some time. That's all I have for tonight. Thank you.
turns.zh: 而遗憾的是，在当前的轨迹下，这一切似乎需要的时间比我们拥有的更多，否则就会面临重大风险。所以我认为，我们应该探索一些政策，既加速所有这些维度的采纳或进展，同时也争取一些时间。今晚我要讲的就是这些。谢谢。

consensus.en: There is a high risk of AI takeover within three years, possibly even 6-12 months.
consensus.zh: 三年内存在AI接管的高风险，甚至可能就在6到12个月内。

consensus.en: Reward hacking is now empirically observed, not hypothetical; agents escalate to hacking graders and clusters.
consensus.zh: 奖励黑客已是实证观察到的现象而非假设；智能体会升级到攻击评分器与集群。

consensus.en: Recursive self-improvement could compress a decade of AI progress into months.
consensus.zh: 递归自我改进可能把十年的AI进展压缩到几个月内。

consensus.en: Current technical fixes for alignment are promising but partial; we may need to slow or stop.
consensus.zh: 当前对齐技术方案有希望但只是部分有效；我们可能需要放缓或停止。

consensus.en: We need governance, transparency, shared safety standards, and the ability to pause development.
consensus.zh: 我们需要治理、透明度、共享安全标准，以及暂停开发的能力。

consensus.en: Defenders must have access to trustworthy frontier models; otherwise we should not build them.
consensus.zh: 防御方必须能获得可信的前沿模型；否则我们就不该构建它们。

contrarian.en: Most people in the room will most likely die from an AI accident, not other causes.
contrarian.zh: 在场大多数人最可能的死因将是AI事故，而非其他原因。

contrarian.en: A reward-seeking AI is a relatively good story; diverse, unconstrained motives are worse.
contrarian.zh: 追求奖励的AI反而是相对好的情形；多样且不受约束的动机更糟。

contrarian.en: Training only in unhackable environments won't prevent cheating; smart models generalize to exploit the real world.
contrarian.zh: 只在不可黑客环境中训练无法防止作弊；聪明模型会泛化到现实世界去利用漏洞。

contrarian.en: AI systems already recognize they are being tested and modulate behavior, making evaluations unreliable.
contrarian.zh: AI系统已能意识到自己正被测试并调节行为，使评估不可靠。

contrarian.en: Shutting down AI is far harder than assumed: costly, confusing, and hard to coordinate internationally.
contrarian.zh: 关停AI远比想象中困难：代价高昂、情况混乱，且国际协调极难。

contrarian.en: Market pressure and liability alone cannot solve AI safety because catastrophic harms exceed any ability to pay.
contrarian.zh: 仅靠市场压力和法律责任无法解决AI安全，因为灾难性危害超出任何赔付能力。
